newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends 25 cts up after narrow range trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends 25 cts up after narrow range trade.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended with a whimper on Thursday after being trapped in a tight one dollar range since the open.

August gas oil closed at $165.25 a tonne, just 25 cents firmer than on Wednesday. September Brent was just a cent firmer at $18.40 a barrel shortly after the gas oil close, after trading in a 12 cent range.
"Nothing happening really," one dealer said. "It is inching a little bit higher, spreads have widened a little - we are just waiting for the Iraqi thing really," one broker said.

Renewed Iraqi oil exports under a U.N. oil-for-food deal, which came into force on June 8, may not emerge until mid August. Oil sales have been delayed while the U.N. considers Baghdad's aid distribution plan.

The $2 billion six-month deal has been split into two three-month, $1 billion tranches and members of the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq said on Thursday Baghdad would not be allowed to change deadlines for the first tranche.
Iraq will not be allowed to carry over more than five percent of its oil allocation from the first tranche into the second.
Industry sources suggest this means Iraq will have to squeeze out 1.5-2.0 million barrels per day to meet its cash target.
